evidence.observation: Binding rule: "The caller route and the packaged route run the same stage loop and the same projection. The packaged shape becomes default data for that code, not a second copy of it (standing rule 4)."

"a shape that names an entity which objectifies a fact type refuses, naming the objectification. The packaged model's `assertion` is such an entity, so the packaged example stays on the packaged path." D10 cost column: "which leaves the packaged model on the old path only". The plan therefore plans two projections, which contradicts R0.4.

evidence.location: §2 LH3 Attached facts, line 231; §2 LH4 Rules, lines 271-273
evidence.observation: "A fact type is attached when one of its roles is played by the assertion entity." and "The packaged pair `(\"asserts\", \"own-finding\")` becomes the default rules, and the comparison at `:122` is removed (R0.4)." In assertion_admission.py:105-113 the packaged rows are `assertion_statement` rows joined to the assertion through the WORK/PASSAGE link facts by (work, passage). The assertion objectifies that fact type and plays no role in it, so under §2's definition it is not attached. A generic requirement over attached fact types cannot express the packaged pair. Lines :122-123 also emit the reasons `negated` or the attribution value, which the H18 stage table pins and LH4-C6 must keep. §2 LH4 instead says a failed requirement "names the requirement".

concerns.recommendation: Make R0.4 consistent with the D10 ruling for admission. Either state that the packaged objectified path stays as its own projection and say which code the two paths share, or state how the packaged shape is expressed as data of the generic projection despite the objectification refusal. State how the default rules reproduce the packaged reason strings and their polarity-first precedence, so that LH3-C8 and LH4-C6 can hold. The LH3 and LH4 specs can then discharge standing rule 4 by name.
concerns.title: Under D10, R0.4's single projection with the packaged shape as default data cannot hold for LH3/LH4

evidence.observation: H5: "every JSON input is capped at 1 MiB; every `gnd` route has 30 seconds and 1 MiB of output (`PROCESS_LIMITS`)". D4 makes only "Five: roster cap (default 128, ceiling 4,096), largest budget (1 MiB, 64 MiB), per-file input (128 KiB, 8 MiB), response (64 KiB, 1 MiB), route timeout (30 s, 600 s)". Neither the JSON decode cap nor the route output cap is a parameter.

"`replay()` re-derives a live LH1 run from its run folder and the caller's input root"; "**LH1-C10** inputs at each roster ceiling load within the spec's time bound". In depth.py:61 `_decode` is fixed at `max_bytes=PROCESS_LIMIT` (1<<20, :22). In reading.py:424 and :435, `_read_retained` reads payload-N.json, which embeds every full response (:192), and the response table through `_read` at INPUT_LIMIT, 128 KiB (depth.py:56). Two default 64 KiB responses therefore push payload-1.json past 128 KiB. Packaged roster rows are 109-141 bytes each, so a roster with 4,096 sources, sections and questions is about 1.6 MB, over the fixed 1 MiB decode cap.

concerns.recommendation: Make D4 cover the JSON decode cap and the route output cap, or derive both from other limits. State which cap replay applies to retained run files: the recorded one or a cap derived from the manifest. Add a criterion that a run at the response and roster ceilings replays, or that run() refuses before the first producer call when its evidence would exceed what replay can read.
concerns.title: Retained evidence can outgrow fixed 1 MiB/128 KiB read caps, so replay cannot read what run writes

evidence.location: §2 LH1 Route exits, lines 190-192; §6 row 'A provider answer crashes the loop after spend'
evidence.observation: "On a caller root the exits of `verify` and `check` over the broad and the targeted population are recorded as observed, 0, 1 or 2, and the run completes (D16, H23)." §6 claims "the order rule and LH1-C11 put every input and model refusal before the first call". docs/reference/rule-check-report.md:87-93 says "the precedence is 1 > 4 > 2 > 0, as for every check" and "| 4 | a must-hold rule is unchecked |". reading.py:270 refuses any exit outside `exits`. A caller model with an unchecked must-hold rule therefore refuses only after every producer call.

concerns.recommendation: State how D16 treats exit 4: record it like 2, or detect it before the first producer call. Cover that case in LH1-C11 or LH1-C13.
concerns.title: D16 lists exits 0/1/2; gnd check's documented exit 4 refuses a caller run after producer spend

evidence.location: §1 H12, H19; §2 LH4 Target cap; §4 LH3-C9
evidence.observation: H12: "`MAX_TARGETS` (`:29`) bounds rows (`:46`) and targets (`:67`)". H19: "about half have other than one actor and one object". LH4: "`max_targets` is an argument from 1 to 1,024." LH3-C9: "1,024 targets with their attached and followed rows project within the spec's time bound." At assertion_admission.py:46, `_rows` refuses any fact type list with `len(value) > MAX_TARGETS`. The plan does not say what bounds attached and followed rows in the generic projection. If the target cap still bounds them, 1,024 claims with two actors each overflow it.

concerns.recommendation: Give the generic projection its own row bound, separate from max_targets, with a ceiling under R0.8. Size LH3-C9 to that bound.
concerns.title: The MAX_TARGETS row bound (:46) has no owner in the generic projection

evidence.observation: R0.5: "Every argument that shapes a caller run is written into the run." LH3: "A call with a shape writes `literature-assertion-admission/2`; the packaged call keeps `/1` (D12)." LH4: "The `/1` record keeps today's statuses, so it keeps its bytes." Nothing says a /2 record binds the shape, the rules document or max_targets, and nothing says which format a call with non-default rules but no shape writes. Today's record (assertion_admission.py:196-200) binds only the model, raw, policy, receipts, report and admitted digests.

concerns.recommendation: State that a /2 record binds the shape, the rules digest and max_targets. State the format and statuses of a rules-only call. Add a criterion that checks both.
concerns.title: Admission shape, rules and max_targets are not said to be bound in the record

evidence.location: §1 H3; §2 LH1 A caller root; §2 LH1 What a caller run writes
evidence.observation: H3 lists "the `unavailable` scenario names `study-methods` (`:448`)". The profile supplies only "the facts added to every population, the producer's label, and the optional review, calibration, conflict and absence steps". evidence.observation: "`document_budget` bounds the bytes read from each source. A document that reaches it has its remaining sections omitted; other documents continue." H8: "the only thing that ends reading early is the byte budget, which omits sections". At reading.py:172-174 the global budget omits only the section that does not fit and continues (`omitted.append(name); continue`), so a later, smaller section is still read. The plan does not say whether the per-document budget skips and continues like this or stops the document, and LH1-C5 cannot tell the two apart.

concerns.recommendation: State whether the per-document budget uses the global skip-if-too-large rule (R0.4) or a hard stop. Give LH1-C5 a fixture with a small section after an oversized one.
concerns.title: Per-document 'reaches it' stop differs from the global budget's skip-and-continue

evidence.location: §5 Compatibility, lines 330-332; §1 H10; §2 LH1 The protocol

response.summary: Digest matches (sha256 6cadaa91…7cb6). One blocking concern. Under the D10 ruling the packaged admission model is refused by the generic shape path, so R0.4's 'same projection, packaged shape as default data' cannot hold for LH3 and LH4 as written. There are six hardening concerns: fixed 1 MiB caps that D4 leaves out, so replay cannot read what a live run writes at scale; check exit 4 missing from D16; the MAX_TARGETS row bound has no owner; admission settings are not bound in the record; the unavailable scenario has no owner on a caller root; the per-document budget's semantics are unclear. The §5 claim about how test_ld3 reaches the producer is also wrong. Most section 1 citations match the checkout. These were checked against source: H1, H2, H3, H4, H6, H7, H8, H12, H13, H15, H16, H17 and H23, and the revision.py citations in H10. H5's depth.py lines and H14's objectified_as lines also match. The plan cites assurance_report.py:757 and :726, but the call is at :760 and the cap at :725. Owner rulings D6, D9, D10 and D17 are not re-argued.
